summary.en: El Salvador has deployed roughly 1,000 troops to Haiti after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince kidnapped four Salvadoran aviation technicians and the bodies recovered were not those hostages. Haitian gangs launched a major attack on UN-backed troops, causing dozens of casualties. The Dominican Republic announced it will not tolerate any gangs within 20km of its border and reinforced its southern frontier to prevent spillover. Heavy rains triggered flooding and landslides that killed four people, adding a humanitarian shock to the security crisis. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: El Salvador har sendt omtrent 1 000 soldater til Haiti etter at en gjengangrep nær Port-au-Prince kidnappet fire salvadoranske luftfartsteknikere, og de funnet kroppene var ikke de bortførte. Haitiske gjenger lanserte et stort angrep på FN-støttede styrker, noe som førte til flere titalls sårede. Den dominikanske republikken kunngjorde at den ikke vil tolerere noen gjenger innen 20 km fra grensen og forsterket sin sørlige grense for å hindre spredning. Kraftig regn forårsaket flom og jordskred som drepte fire personer, og la til et humanitært sjokk i sikkerhetskrisen. Konflikten ga 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
